+# Postmortem: BookMetadataTrafficStalled + BooklogrApiLatencyP99High
+
+## Incident Summary
+Two alerts fired simultaneously:
+1. **BookMetadataTrafficStalled** (warning) — book-metadata inbound request rate collapsed from normal levels to ~0.035 req/s
+2. **BooklogrApiLatencyP99High** (critical) — p99 latency spiked to ~5s (threshold: 300ms)
+
+## Root Cause
+Commit `e8c2043` ("Order library list by shelf position") replaced the SQL-level pagination in `GET /v1/books` with a full table scan + in-memory sort.
+
+**Before (working):**
+```python
+books = books.paginate(page=offset, per_page=limit, error_out=False)
+```
+The database handled sorting (`ORDER BY`) and pagination (`LIMIT/OFFSET`), returning only the requested page of results.
+
+**After (broken):**
+```python
+ranked = sorted(books.all(), key=_rank, reverse=(order == "desc"))
+page_items = ranked[start:start + per_page]
+```
+Every request to `GET /v1/books` loaded **all** rows from the database into Python, then sorted them in-memory using a custom `_rank` function (with accent-folding via `unicodedata`). This turned an O(page_size) indexed query into an O(N·log N) full-table scan + Python sort on every request.
+
+### Cascading Impact
+The slow `get_books` requests monopolized all gunicorn worker processes. With workers blocked on these multi-second requests, no capacity remained to serve `search_books` requests — which are the endpoint that calls the book-metadata provider. This explains the **BookMetadataTrafficStalled** alert: the upstream consumer (booklogr-api) effectively stopped calling book-metadata because its workers were saturated.
+
+## Evidence
+| Signal | Value | Source |
+|--------|-------|--------|
+| p99 latency | 4.97s | `histogram_quantile(0.99, ...)` Prometheus query |
+| book-metadata request rate | 0.035/s (collapsed) | `rate(book_metadata_requests_total[2m])` |
+| All responses HTTP 200 | No 5xx errors | `sum by (status)(rate(...))` |
+| Commit date | 2026-07-21 09:28:07 UTC | `git log` — deployed ~1 min before first alert |
+| Changed file | `api/routes/books.py` | `git show --stat e8c2043` |
+
+## Fix Applied
+Reverted commit `e8c2043` via `git revert --no-edit e8c2043`, restoring the original SQL-level `ORDER BY` + `paginate()` implementation.
+
+## Action Items
+- [ ] Add a load test for `GET /v1/books` with realistic data volumes before merging sort changes
+- [ ] Implement connection/worker saturation alerting to catch this pattern earlier
+- [ ] If shelf-position sorting is still desired, implement it via SQL expressions (`CASE`, collation) rather than Python-side full-table loads
